note: Adapted from the new-species description of Sands 1965 (in English); the alate, the large soldier and the small soldier are described, with no separate worker; type locality Sibasa, Transvaal, South Africa. The mean head width of the large soldier is blurred by the OCR (printed 0.80), so only the range is given. The OCR mistook decimal points for hyphens or colons (I-16 is 1.16, 0:35 is 0.35), restored here by order of magnitude; where a mean is unclear only the range is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldiers dimorphic (large and small); differs from F. contractus in the more rounded posterior lobes of the soldier head capsule and the usually more distinct points of the mandibular vestiges, and in the shape of the right mandible of the alate and the different setae of the vertex; also separable from F. tenebricus by the right mandible.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule extremely dark brown, almost ink black, postclypeus and antennae (except the yellowish brown basal 2 segments) dark brown, posterior part of the labrum brown becoming yellow towards the apex; pronotum of the same colour as the head capsule, meso- and metanotum and the remaining thoracic sclerites and the legs dark brown, only the tarsi and the tips of the tibiae yellow to yellowish brown; abdominal sclerites dark brown, the midline of the anterior sternites paler; wings translucent brown, darker at the base, with a slight greenish sheen, veins dark brown or outlined in dark brown at the base. Posterior margin of the head capsule behind the eyes nearly a semicircle; frontal mark very small, short Y-shaped, varying in paleness, in some males almost effaced; compound eyes angularly oval, not protruding, rather small relative to the head width, eye width index 3.5—3.8; ocelli small, oval, separated from the compound eye by from 1/4 to twice their own minimum diameter; postclypeus strongly inflated, 1.9—2.0 times as wide as long, anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin convex and rounded; antennae 14—15-segmented, usually 14-segmented, II, V and VI subequal and longer than IV, III twice IV and often partly divided; the posterior cutting edge of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible exposed beyond the second marginal tooth and rather long, the molar surface moderately concave at the base, with 8 ridges. Female cerci as long as their basal width, slightly mammillo-conical. Vertex with 1—2 long bristle-like setae and sparsely scattered short hairs, with a few further bristle-like setae around the compound eyes and ocelli. Measurements (11 individuals, 5 localities, mm): head width (across the eyes) 1.12—1.19 (mean 1.16); maximum diameter of the compound eye 0.31—0.33 (mean 0.32); ocellus 0.06—0.09 × 0.09—0.11 (mean 0.08 × 0.10); ocellus to eye 0.13—0.15 (mean 0.13); pronotum width 1.02—1.17 (mean 1.08); pronotum length 0.71—0.79 (mean 0.74); hind tibia length 1.38—1.45 (mean 1.41); forewing length 8.20—9.60 (mean 8.99).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large soldier: head capsule orange to rusty red, nasus rusty orange to ink black (paler at the apex); pronotum, antennae and abdominal tergites brown to dark brown, femora brown, tibiae and tarsi yellow, sternites pale brown. Head capsule in frontal view constricted behind the antennae, the posterior margin regularly rounded; nasus conical; in lateral view straight or slightly concave from behind the antennal base, then suddenly raised and curving smoothly into the occiput, the nasus shorter than the rest of the head capsule, nasus cone angle 15—20 degrees; antennae 13-segmented, II and IV subequal and shorter than V, III and VI subequal and longer than V; setae: 6—8 at the tip of the nasus and 1 pair of small setae on the vertex, the dorsum with only very few scattered minute setae. Small soldier: colour and setae as in the large soldier; head capsule in frontal view more sharply constricted behind the antennae; in lateral view concave, slightly wavy or sunken in front of the smaller posterior lobes; nasus shorter than or equal to the rest of the head capsule, nasus cone angle 10—17 degrees; antennae 12—13-segmented, usually 13-segmented. Large soldier measurements (14 individuals, 8 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.43—1.61 (mean 1.52); head width 0.78—0.89; head capsule depth 0.54—0.66 (mean 0.58); pronotum width 0.41—0.49 (mean 0.43); pronotum length 0.18—0.23 (mean 0.19); hind tibia length 1.00—1.17 (mean 1.08). Small soldier measurements (14 individuals, 8 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.28—1.44 (mean 1.33); head width 0.56—0.66 (mean 0.61); head capsule depth 0.41—0.49 (mean 0.45); pronotum width 0.33—0.37 (mean 0.35); pronotum length 0.13—0.18 (mean 0.15); hind tibia length 0.82—1.02 (mean 0.94).
